lines.text: The measuring began at dawn, in the thickest smoke Tobin's lanterns could make.
One ring. Next.
Oswin's lessons were paying off. Mostly.
Oof. So heavy.
Mostly.
One ring. Are you ill, blacksmith?
It's the smoke, miss. Ancient tradition. Very bad for the chest.
Hask didn't measure anyone himself. He just watched, smiling, sipping tea from a cup somebody had given him. It was much worse than if he'd shouted.
Ah. The steward. Allow me.
He took off his glove. He wasn't going to use a lens at all.
He reads by touch. The way I do. Smoke won't help.
Hask took Bram's one hand in his.
Since midwinter, Oswin had been teaching Bram to hold his aether in. Like holding your breath, all the way down. Bram called it nonsense. He had practised every single night anyway.
Nobody in the square breathed.
Two rings. A strong two.
I've worked hard, Magister.
Told you the breathing was good for you.
Shut up, Oswin.
So rings could be hidden. Not erased. Not faked. Just held, like a breath. And if Bram could hold five rings down to two, what else could we hide?
Across the square, Hask raised his teacup to me. As if we had both just played a very good move.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter twenty, coming soon.
